title: RIP Natural Hypertrophy; Welcome School of Strategy!
summary: After losing his job and refusing ads or sponsors, NH announces the School of Strategy, named after Musashi. It has a 'strategist' mentorship tier for hypertrophy and self-improvement, built to make clients independent, and a 'seeker' tier of literature and philosophy lessons. He sets out who the service fits and who it doesn't, and explains his mentor-not-coach philosophy.
claims: He started the channel after his wife told him that if he didn't start today he never would
He ran the channel unmonetised as a hobby for about five years, then used Ko-fi pledges to offset overtime when he became his family's sole provider
Working 50-60 hour weeks left him unable to make videos, causing a three-month gap last spring
His employer let him go without reason, leaving him with time but only about a quarter of his former income
He refuses ads and sponsorships on principle: principles you drop as soon as they get uncomfortable were never principles
He dislikes the label 'coach'; his goal is to teach people to think, program and coach themselves, not to make them dependent

The strategist tier covers physique reviews, personalised programs built from favourite lifts, injury history, frequency, split and equipment, and programs aimed at a 'goal physique' from art or fiction
If your circumstances change, he provides a flexible backup plan for the new training environment to preserve gains
He priced the tier well below typical coaching so students and people with little money can join
He expects most people to stay 4 months to a year before graduating and becoming independent
He reserves the right to drop and refund clients who show no willingness or no interest in becoming independent
Coaches who change your program every week to justify their fees are counterproductive for bodybuilding
His help is purely reactive with no scheduled check-ins; if a client goes a month without asking anything, he takes that as a sign they don't need him
He gives no strict diet plans, only advice on whether to bulk, cut or recomp and how long and how fast
His expertise is bodybuilding and hypertrophy; you will get stronger, but he won't coach strength as a goal, contest prep or posing
He does not believe in non-responders: there is always a reason behind stagnation, and it is never you or your genetics
He has helped many people labelled non-responders make gains after years of plateau
Former strongmen and powerlifters in their 30s-40s, often injured, moving to bodybuilding for health and looks are a good fit
Novices don't need a coach: eat more and follow a free program, and anything works for them; paying for coaching mostly wastes their money
The seeker tier is 4 hours a month of literature and philosophy lessons, in conversation or essay format, capped at 10 students
Complete beginners in philosophy should read on their own and use free YouTube content rather than pay for lessons
He prices so that consistency is rewarded: a long-term student paying 30% less is better than an occasional one paying 30% more
Without ads or sponsors he can make whatever content he wants, from four-hour philosophy videos to long storytime streams
